:::{#def-prediction-bias}
#### Bias of a prediction

Let $\fitproc$ be a [fitting procedure](#def-fitting-procedure),
and let $\trainset$ be a random [training set](#def-training-set).
At a covariate value $\predvar$,
the prediction $\predvalf{\predvar}$ is a random variable,
because it depends on the random training data.
Let $\paren{\newpredvar, \newoutvar}$ be a [new observation](#def-new-observation) with $\newpredvar = \predvar$.
The **bias** of the prediction
is the expected [prediction error](prediction.qmd#def-prediction-error)
of the prediction $\predvalf{\predvar}$ of the new outcome $\newoutvar$.
The expectation averages over [training sets](#def-training-set) and over the new outcome:

$$
\bias{\predvalf{\predvar}}
= \E{\prederr_{*}\paren{\fitmodf{\trainset}} \mid \newpredvar = \predvar}.
$$ {#eq-prediction-bias}

:::
